business: Alpine Bloom Landscape & Facilities, Inc. (Commercial Landscaping, Irrigation & Snow Removal)

redFlags: Related-party equipment lease above market: Partially supportable. The equipment is leased from an entity the owner controls. Only the above-market element of roughly $92,000 is a genuine adjustment; the buyer still has to pay a market rate for mowers, loaders and plow trucks it needs to operate.

Heavy winter overtime claimed as non-recurring: Unsupported. Snow is the business. The seller adds back overtime from a heavy winter while keeping all of the snow revenue that overtime generated, which is a one-sided normalisation.

Loss of Selkirk Health portfolio (buyer adjustment): Buyer-identified downward adjustment. Management discloses in the Q&A that its largest grounds-maintenance customer gave notice of non-renewal after the TTM period closed. The roughly $171,000 of contribution that account carried is not in the forward business and must come out of the number a buyer capitalises.
yellowFlags: Owner compensation above market: Partially supportable. About $146,000 of the $222,000 claim exceeds the cost of an operations manager and an estimator to cover the owner's role.
Fleet telematics rollout: Fully supportable. A discrete two-month installation with no other activity in the account across the three-year ledger.
Customer concentration: Largest customer, Blue Heron Development Co., is 15.8% of FY2025 revenue; top 5 are 62.8%.

Seasonality and net working capital swing: FY2025 monthly EBITDA ranges from $-38,415 to $223,052; cash ranges from $2,722,435 to $3,636,021. The NWC peg must be set on a 12-month average, not a period-end snapshot.
greenFlags: Verified TTM Revenue of $9.47M across VDR financials.
Reported TTM EBITDA of $1.63M reconciled against tax returns and bank statements.
